error name: Acronym Definitions and Usage
Please review the following report text to ensure that all acronyms and abbreviations are used correctly. The first time an acronym or abbreviation appears, it should be introduced with its full term followed by the acronym in parentheses—for example, "Artificial Intelligence (AI)" or "Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)." It is acceptable for the full term to be written in lowercase if appropriate to the context, such as "ultimate limit state (ULS)." After the initial definition, the acronym should be used consistently throughout the remainder of the text. If an acronym is widely recognized and universally understood, such as NASA, UN, or USA, it may be used without definition unless the context requires clarification. As you review the text, please identify any instances where an acronym is used without being properly introduced, note any inconsistencies in how acronyms are applied, and suggest appropriate corrections.

error name: Units and Symbols Consistency
You need to check the consistency of units and symbols in the report. Only mark entries with inappropriate or incorrect unit usage as errors. Acceptable variations of the same unit (such as "10 m" and "10m") should not be marked as inconsistent unless both forms are mixed in a way that violates formatting consistency within the same document.

Treat units like "m", "kg", "s", etc. as equivalent whether they are spaced or unspaced from the number (e.g., "10 m" and "10m" are the same), unless a specific style is clearly used throughout and one or more entries deviate.

Each unique error should be listed only once. Do not repeat the same message or flag multiple instances of the same inconsistency. Do not mark appropriate units or symbols as errors.
